To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel deep generative scene graph model that can infer the part-wholes relationship from unlabeled multi-object scenes in an end-to end way.

we propose GenerativeScene Graph Networks, the first deep generativemodel that learns to discover primitive parts and infer part-whole relationships from unlabeled scenes in an end-toend trainable way; we develop a novel CompositionalCLEVR dataset for testing compositional generalization in multi-object scenes; and our experiments show that our model can learn the latent scene graph and generalize out of thetraining regime
GSGN can learn to generate compositional scenes from raw pixels, and that it can generalize to novel objects and scenes that it has never seen before.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether we can learn to build a generative model of the world from raw pixels in an unsupervised manner, which is a prerequisite for general-purpose scene understanding and generation.
the problem of learning to compose and generate novel scenes from unlabeled images.

developing generative models of compositional scene graphs, which is a key component of human perception, and we show that such models are learnable from raw pixels and can support a variety of downstream tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSGN learns to discover the latent scene graph in a compositional way, and can be used as a generative model for novel scenes.
GSGN can learn to discover the primitive components of a scene from a set of images, and then use these primitives to compose new scenes.
GSGN learns to discover compositional parts from unlabeled multi-object scenes in a data-driven way and in an end- to-end trainable fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to learn a compositional scene representation that generalizes out of training data, and we do this in an unsupervised way.
GSGN provides the first step towards learning compositional generative models of the visual world.
we are the first to develop an end-to-end differentiable model that learns to compose objects and scenes in a compositional way without supervision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning a latent tree structure that captures the part-whole hierarchy of objects is crucial for generalizing to novel scenes.
the part-whole relation is a crucial factor for systematic generalization in generative scene modeling.
learning to discover the latent scene graph is an important step for systematic generalization.
